Team — copying the thread below. Northstar (deal D-48721) has two specific asks that need legal/security sign-off before we push the order form live: SOC2 evidence cadence and pen-test/inspection language. They want to close mid-November.

Key asks from Claire (external):
- Confirm frequency and contents of evidence (SOC 2 + quarterly summary)
- Define inspection access: notice period, environment (staging vs prod), and allowed artifacts

My proposed position (to keep procurement velocity while protecting our IP and uptime):
1) Evidence: provide SOC 2 Type II report upon signature; maintain an "evidence bundle" quarterly that includes any material control changes, a redacted summary of recent pen test findings, and an availability/incident summary for the quarter. We do NOT provide full raw logs or customer-specific telemetry.
2) Pen test / inspection: accept remote, time-boxed pen tests against an isolated staging environment only. Notice: 48 business hours for scoped tests; 10 business days for any broad, manual inspection. Any test requiring access to production-level telemetry or extended testing windows will require an on-site agreement and a scoped statement of work (SOW) with a dedicated engineer and pre-approved IP protections.
3) SLAs & blackout windows: offer a 2-hour maintenance blackout window per day for staging access and require that tests avoid Redwood release windows (we will provide release schedule snapshots as part of quarterly bundle).

Attachments I'm proposing to send to Northstar: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2028.pdf (redacted), pen_test_scope_draft.docx (scope template with explicit disallowed testing), and a short decision log that we keep internal.

Can you please:
- Karthik: draft concise exhibit language (2-3 paragraphs) that maps to (1)-(3) above and protects us from unlimited inspection claims. Flag any non-starters.
- Laura: confirm that staging environment access and our recommended notice windows align with operational reality; add any technical constraints we must call out.
- Vanessa: confirm whether the proposed evidence bundle cadence conflicts with standard legal asks for enterprise customers and whether we should offer an optional paid SOW for extended inspection needs.

If we can get language and a single consolidated redline by EOD 11/9 I can push the updated exhibit to Northstar and keep the go-live cadence.

Thanks —
Rishi

Thanks for pulling this together, Rishi. Agreed with the high-level approach — below are my suggested contract paragraphs and operational call-outs. I am attaching a quick redline but pasting the suggested language here so we can iterate quickly.

Suggested exhibit language (draft):
1) SOC 2 and Evidence. Upon execution of the Agreement, Redwood Inference will provide Customer with its most recent SOC 2 Type II report and thereafter a quarterly evidence summary containing: (i) redacted summaries of control changes materially affecting security; (ii) a summary of recent third-party penetration testing activities and remediation status; and (iii) service availability metrics for the preceding quarter. Customer acknowledges that Redwood does not provide or retain customer-specific raw logs as part of routine evidence.

2) Penetration Testing and Inspections. Customer may request time-limited penetration testing against a Redwood-managed staging environment subject to the following: (i) Customer shall provide at least two (2) business days' prior written notice for scoped tests; (ii) any broad or production-impacting inspection shall require a minimum of ten (10) business days' prior written notice and an executed SOW; (iii) Redwood may require a dedicated technical liaison and reasonable security controls (e.g., time-limited accounts, IP allowlisting) during testing. Testing that attempts to exfiltrate customer or third-party data, bypass authentication, or cause sustained load impacting production systems is expressly prohibited.

3) Operational Coordination and Blackouts. Parties will coordinate testing windows with Redwood's release calendar; Redwood will provide release snapshots quarterly and maintain routine blackout periods to protect live operations. Any test that materially risks service availability will be subject to immediate suspension by Redwood.

Operational notes:
- Laura: staging environment is available for scoped tests; we require signed NDAs for contractor testers and a short onboarding checklist (I left a comment in the redline on where to reference).
- Vanessa: recommend offering an "Extended Inspection SOW" add-on for customers who need production-level checks; price as professional services to avoid precedent of unlimited inspections.
